item.title: Man Utd held to goalless draw at Everton
item.description: Manchester United's 12 points from their opening eight Women's Super League games is their lowest ever at this stage of a season [Getty Images] In-form Manchester United made it 10 games unbeaten in all competitions, but were held by Everton to a drab goalless draw at Goodison Park. Despite a good run of results, Eva Olid's United side are yet to fully fire offensively in the Women's Super League and were mostly neutralised by Scott Phelan's well-organised Everton team. Norway striker Elisabeth Terland came close to a late United winner, latching on to Jess Park's through ball with 15 minutes left but she was denied by a fine save from Courtney Brosnan. At the other end, Everton's Ornella Vignola had earlier passed up two decent opportunities when she shot straight at Phallon Tullis-Joyce. Olid has found her attacking formula in the new-look League Cup, with United scoring 22 goals in four matches, albeit three of those games coming against lower-league opposition. However, with just nine WSL goals so far this season, the lowest through seven games in United's history, it was perhaps unsurprising that Everton would prove tough opponents. Since Phelan took charge in January, only Arsenal and Chelsea have kept more clean sheets and their combination of pressing and a high defensive line nullified the visitors. It is at the other end where Everton are less effective with recalled Dutch striker Rosa van Gool isolated for much of the 90 minutes. The result leaves United four points off third place and the Champions League qualification spots. That berth is currently occupied by London City Lionesses, who host champions Manchester City in Sunday's blockbuster Women's Super League match (12:00 GMT). United broke with ferocity and Mbeumo’s beautiful ball across found Fernandes in oceans of space, but he blazed over on his left foot. Shortly after, Fernandes fired a dangerous ball across goal that just missed Mbeumo as the visitors turned up the heat. item.title: Our part of Mbappe, China issue over: Real Madrid's Mourinho
item.description: Kylian Mbappe has faced criticism in China for his comment and Spanish football is not being shown on state television as a result (Oscar DEL POZO) Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho said Saturday the club's involvement in the controversy over Kylian Mbappe's comments about an internet meme about himself and former Chinese leader Mao Zedong was over, after both the player and club apologised. Mbappe's remarks sparked a backlash in China, with Real Madrid, the France forward and La Liga all issuing apologies, but Chinese state television nevertheless pulled Spanish football from its schedules. In a clip from an interview with French show "The Bridge" which has since been taken down, Mbappe had said he was amused by an internet meme showing his face photoshopped onto "some guy, think he's a Chinese dictator", an apparent reference to Mao. Mourinho said both Mbappe and 15-time European champions Real Madrid "had the class" to issue swift apologies and believes there is nothing more for them to do. "I've seen a lot of responsibility from a club which, at this level, is a club of great class, and as far as we're concerned, that's it, we've done our part, there's nothing more for us to do," Mourinho told reporters. Mocking former leader Mao -- blamed by historians for millions of deaths -- is taboo in China, and the 27-year-old's remarks saw him become the latest foreign sports figure to anger Beijing. "With this situation involving China, these are the dangers of today's world, where many times the best thing you can do is keep your mouth shut, because there's danger in so many things you say or comment on," said Mourinho. Mbappe has endured a difficult week, after he finished second behind Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane in Monday's Ballon d'Or ceremony. Mourinho praised Mbappe's reaction after England international Kane was named the world's best player. "Kylian is very intelligent, very mature, with a very high level of self-esteem," said Mourinho. "At the same time, he shows real class in the way he's interpreted the Ballon d'Or going to Harry. In him I've only seen and felt class and respect. "One thing is knowing you're the best, and another is having respect for those who have also done a lot to win a trophy. From him I only see class." Mourinho said midfielder Jude Bellingham coming in 11th in the voting left him with his "mouth open", implying the Englishman should have finished far higher. However, the veteran Portuguese coach, who worked with Kane at Tottenham between 2019 and 2021, said he was happy for the Bayern hitman. "I had the privilege of working with Harry, he's a great player and a great professional and a great person," added Mourinho. "Inside the frustration that my player (Mbappe) didn't win, well, I have to be honest and say I'm very happy for Harry, a player and a boy who deserves it." rbs/nf

Alonso was without Reece James, Emiliano Martínez and João Pedro. They have managed just two wins this season, against Ipswich and Sabah, the latter in September. United remain one point above the relegation zone , but have played a game more. item.description: UNITED STATES - JUNE 19: Baseball: St, Louis Cardinals Randy Flores in action, pitching vs Tampa Bay Devil Rays, St, Petersburg, FL 6/19/2005 (Photo by Tom DiPace/Sports Illustrated via Getty Images) I usually wait at least a night to comment on huge news items like this. Immediate reactions bring rash statements one way or another. Ultimately, there are three competing narrativs when it comes to the hire of Randy Flores as general manager and all three narratives have kernels of truth in them. So, all of them are right and all of them are wrong perhaps in equal measure. Essentially, we have the glass half full approach, glass half empty approach, and the middle ground approach. We will look at each one by one. Glass Half Full If one looks at the failures of the Astros organization in recent seasons, one can look no further than the disintegration of the minor league system. Obviously, there are a number of factors that play into that. Every major league team lost much of the 2020 draft due to COVID. Then, the league took the Astros first and second round picks for two seasons because of the sign stealing scandal. Then, you have to use of prospects in trades to keep the championship window open. So, saying the Astros’ farm system was terrible is not a complete indictment of Dana Brown or James Click before him. However, Flores comes over primarily with a player development background. Baseball America ranked the Cardinals as the number two overall farm system in MLB coming into 2026. They had them ranked towards the middle of the pack for much of the previous decade where they ranked as low as 20th and as high as ninth. The Astros never ranked better than 24th in the same time. Fangraphs had the Cardinals ranked fourth last season. So, multiple sources considered the Cardinals to be among the best farm systems in baseball. Flores began his work in 2015 officially, but was already gaining marks for innovation before he joined the Cardinals. That would seem to compliment the Driveline executives the Astros just brought in. It is impossible to know whether any move will be positive in the moment, but at least Flores was sought after by other clubs. He had interviewed in Baltimore and was listed as a prime candidate in Anaheim as well. This is as opposed to Dana Brown who was not a candidate anywhere other than Houston before he was hired. item.title: John Harbaugh violated norms, called Titans ownership about Jeffery Simmons
item.description: John Harbaugh | Getty Images New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh took the extraordinary step of calling Tennessee Titans ownership directly in an effort to acquire star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, according to a startling report from Jonathan Jones of The Athletic . Per Jones, that breaks with “traditional NFL trade-talk norms” where general managers deal directly with each other. Jones reported that Harbaugh contacted Titans owner Amy Adams Strunk after Giants GM Joe Schoen had been told by Titans GM Mike Borgonzi that Simmons, a 29-year-old four-time Pro Bowler and 2025 First-Team All-Pro, would not be traded. Strunk apparently gave Harbaugh the same message. That obviously changed when the Chicago Bears made a Godfather offer to the Titans of two first-round and a fourth-round draft pick. Per Jones, one GM said Harbaugh’s call to Strunk “violates a code amongst primary football decision-makers, that they will only deal with each other.” Valentine’s View Whether Harbaugh violated NFL traditions or not, the move tells you a couple of things about the Giants. This is clearly Harbaugh’s show. We have told you that before, but this is absolutely evidence that Harbaugh is front-and-center in every major decision, and that he will do whatever he believes necessary to get something done. Even if that steps on toes. The Giants are clearly intent upon seizing the opportunity they have in the NFC East. Forget building. Harbaugh wants the Giants to be the best they can be right now, and if there is a star player out there like Simmons or running back Jonathan Taylor who can help make that happen, the Giants will try to get it done. Whether going for it right now is the correct approach, after the Giants have spent most of the last 15 years floundering you have to appreciate the boldness. I think it is also important to note that Simmons and Taylor, who is now reportedly available , are players who would be more than short-term, 2026 upgrades. One other note in terms of surrendering draft capital. Whether it is too early for a Jaxson Dart vs. J.J. McCarthy debate, the Giants clearly understand that if they spend draft capital now, they possess two desirable, 23-year-old quarterbacks and they can use one in the offseason to recoup premium draft picks.

item.title: Chelsea 2-0 Manchester United: Positive start wasted by Martinez, defensive stupidity
item.description: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 31: Lisandro Martinez of Manchester United leaves the pitch after receiving a red card during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Chelsea FC and Manchester United at Stamford Bridge on October 31, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images) The chaos spiral continues at Manchester United as Michael Carrick’s side found a new way to let down the manager and fans. The Reds battled through a testy first half at Stamford Bridge in which the side should have scored. If they had, what came next might not have stung quite as much. The second half display could not have been further from “battling,” and resulted in a second straight Premier League defeat to make it seven points through nine matches. The defense was solid in the first half of action, though there were still worrying moments in transition. The best moments for Chelsea came from players being caught out of position, with Diogo Dalot notably sloppy on a United corner to give up a disallowed goal. United were the team on the front foot, though, and should have done better with some decent chances. Amad and Matheus Cunha both had shots on target blocked or put off balance while Bruno Fernandes whiffed on a tremendous chance created by Bryan Mbeumo. The winger sent him through with an excellent pass into the left half space, but Bruno’s shot was too powerful and sent high into the air. Bruno nearly set up Mbeumo as well with a low, driven cross through the box towards the back post, but his teammate was just a bit too late to tap it into the net. The positivity was warranted after the first half, but the second half could not have gone to hell much quicker than it did. Chelsea were put in front by Morgan Rogers shortly after the restart. A poor turnover of possession near the center circle turned into a gallop through acres of space in the heart of the United team. Harry Maguire was left backpedaling and accounting for an open Estevao to Rogers’ left, and was depending on Lisandro Martinez for help. Instead, the Argentine was caught ball watching as Rogers continued his run through the center and slotted a simple shot past Senne Lammens. Poor cohesion and awareness led to the goal, and a frustrating switchoff led to the second as Martinez gave away a penalty. He recklessly shoved a Chelsea player without even looking at the ball on a corner kick cross. To make matters worse, he did so shortly after receiving a yellow card, and was sent off for a second bookable offense. Cole Palmer converted the penalty and the result was all but settled. Chelsea should have had a third, but Estevao was just offside when he beat Maguire in a 3v1 situation. The Blues were nearly gifted another goal as Joshua Zirkzee attempted a ridiculous tap around a defender on the dribble. The problem was that Zirkzee was still well in his own half and United were pinned back, meaning his showy move was easily intercepted by the sieging Chelsea players. Uni

FC Köln: Hosts looking for immediate revenge after midweek thrashing Union Berlin Union Berlin currently sit 16th in the table and also failed to win last weekend against Augsburg away from home getting a 1-1 draw. item.title: College Football Fans Pay Big Price For Dirty Chants
item.description: William Purnell-Imagn Images UCF fans learned a hard lesson last Saturday night after their team beat BYU in double overtime. The University of Central Florida got slapped with a $100,000 fine because some fans yelled hurtful slurs at the visiting team. This is not just a slap on the wrist; it is a clear message that hate speech has no place in our stadiums. The Big 12 Conference made sure everyone knows that behavior will not be tolerated again. The trouble started during a wild 39-31 win in Orlando. According to The Sun , students were heard chanting a four-letter word followed by “the Mormons” right before the game. The Acrisure Bounce House holds 45,906 people, and the noise from those hateful chants drowned out the spirit of good sportsmanship. Students were kicked out of the stadium immediately after the mess started. The Price of Bad Behavior The Big 12 did not wait around to decide what to do. The Conference released a statement saying they recognize UCF tried to handle the problem during the game. They noted that some people responsible for the conduct were removed right away. The fine of $100,000 will go straight to student education initiatives instead of staying in the school’s pocket. This money is meant to teach a lesson that lasts longer than one game. A $100,000 fine directed toward student education initiatives was issued to UCF by the Conference, as reported by the US Sun. This is a huge sum for a college program to lose over a few minutes of noise. It shows that the league is serious about protecting its reputation and the people who play in it. Any other incidents of misbehavior going forward will result in further penalties for UCF. One strike is bad, but two strikes could cost the team their season. New Rules for the Whole League This isn’t just about UCF; it changes things for every team in the conference. The league knows that one bad night can hurt everyone. Effective immediately, the Big 12 is implementing an updated Conference-wide policy with escalating consequences for discriminatory conduct at athletic events, in conjunction with this action. That means every school from now on has to watch their fans closer than before. The rules are stricter, and the punishments will get worse fast if anyone breaks them again. I have raised four kids and now I spoil my grandbabies, and I know a thing or two about teaching respect. You can be loud and proud for your team without being mean to others. Cheering for your Knights is fine, but you do not get to scream slurs at people of faith. The $100,000 fine is a start, but the real test is whether UCF fans will change their ways next time.

item.title: Caleb Williams’s Cleat Maker: Hiding Logos After NFL Fines ‘Makes Sense’
item.description: Close to 100 NFL players wear the same brand of cleats that Bears quarterback Caleb Williams has worn while incurring two recent fines by the league totaling nearly $36,000 for displaying unauthorized logos during games, the company’s founder and CEO tells Front Office Sports . Jack Rasmussen told FOS that he aspires for his small company, Caddix, to grow into someday being an authorized brand for NFL players to display the logos during games, but that’s not affordable at this point. In the meantime, he acknowledged it may be practical for Williams to continue to wear the cleats but cover or remove the logos to avoid further fines, as NFL rules permit. “I think that makes sense,” Rasmussen told FOS on Friday. “Like I said, I mean, the whole fine situation makes sense. So if what’s going to happen and what needs to happen to keep him on the field and for the cameras to be out of his face, to hide the logo … I think that’s what needs to happen. I don’t agree with it. But I think down the road, you know, hiding the logo is kind of one of the … numerous options that we have to remedy the situation.” Williams has appealed at least one of his fines and has a hearing scheduled for Nov. 10, according to Rasmussen. “So we’ll kind of see what shakes out from that,” Rasmussen said. “We’re kind of taking it a day at a time. It’s kind of unprecedented in a way. The appeals don’t really happen for logos, I’m told. That’s more of about a targeting or a hip-drop [tackle] or something like that. But this is kind of rare air we’re breathing.” Williams was fined $23,882 by the NFL for the unauthorized logo on the Caddix cleats that he wore in Week 7, three sources confirmed Thursday to FOS . That fine was first reported by ProFootballTalk . Williams’s initial fine was $11,941. NFL rules prohibit a player from displaying a non-approved logo on footwear. The NFL’s authorized footwear suppliers are Adidas, Nike, and Under Armour. A limited number of players are permitted to wear footwear with the Air Jordan brand. A player can opt to wear footwear from another company but, if so, must have all visible third-party names, logos, brands, and other commercial identification removed or covered, which is known as spatting. Unfortunately, an offside goal from Estêvão was all we had to show for that early impetus, the youngster tapping in after the goalkeeper gave up a rebound, but finding himself well behind the defensive line on the initial shot. After those opening 15 minutes however, Manchester United started coming into the game and Chelsea were suddenly and distinctly second-best. It’s not that United were amazing, but we had lost our confidence and errors were being made all over the pitch — including in critical areas. Thankfully, we somehow escaped without conceding, as multiple big chances went begging for the visitors. They did have the ball in the back of our net briefly, from a corner, but had it ruled out for an offside. Chelsea did find our footing in the final few minutes of the period but the half-time whistle was a welcome arrival. item.title: Skip Bayless urges Jerry Jones to trade for ‘baller’ to make the Cowboys contenders
item.description: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images Jerry Jones has invested heavily in this year’s Dallas Cowboys team by giving up a lot of picks to get better for the here and now. It has certainly been a rocky start to the 2026 season for the Cowboys, given they sit second in what has been a far-from-impressive NFC East. However, there is an opportunity there to get into the playoffs as they sit just shy of the New York Giants. The trade deadline is now just a matter of days away and the NFC has already seen some mammoth trades made this week. The Cowboys have not flinched in the market since signing Joey Porter Jr. but there is potential for Jones to make a splash. Skip Bayless still believes more is needed in Dallas to truly make them contenders this season, but there is one player on his mind that could swing the momentum back in Dallas’ favour. Skip Bayless urges Jerry Jones to trade for Maxx Crosby Maxx Crosby’s future with the Las Vegas Raiders is being speculated about again after their form fell off a cliff following the opening three games. However, this is a trade that would require Jones to part with a lot of picks to bring in the excellent defender. “Go get Max Crosby. I know there are rumours all over the internet about it, but nothing tangible or credible. I do, because we don’t have a difference maker who’s a leader, a gamer, and a baller. As a pass rusher, we don’t have that. We got Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark in the interior, and we got a few pieces on the edge, but Max Crosby is a cornerstone to me. He’s 29, and you’d have him at his peak for a couple more years, probably,” said Bayless on Smith’s YouTube channel. “Man, if you add Max Crosby and Joey Porter Jr. to this defence, now we’re credible, now we’re solid where we haven’t been solid. The schedule is screaming for us to go win the East and see if we could actually win a playoff game this year. That’s what I would do.” There will be a lot of debate as to whether Crosby is willing to leave Las Vegas now following the debacle he endured during the offseason with the Baltimore Ravens. Having only completed two sacks this season, there may also be questions as to whether teams will be looking for a discount on what Crosby was set to cost the Ravens earlier this year. The Ravens agreed to send two first-round picks to Vegas for Crosby before pulling the plug on the deal. Given the 29-year-old has not quite been at his absolute best, there is potential for there to be some conflict in negotiating a possible trade for Crosby at this stage of the season. item.description: Racing Bulls team principal Alan Permane has rejected Max Verstappen 's claim that Liam Lawson picked a fight with him during second practice for the Mexico City Grand Prix . The two Red Bull family drivers had a feisty exchange in the stadium section on Friday at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez, going wheel to wheel and then colliding at the penultimate corner. The incident saw the FP2 session red-flagged and left Verstappen with damage he had to carry for the remaining 45 minutes. Verstappen was far from impressed by his former Red Bull teammate, whose F1 future remains in question despite strong performances this season. Addressing the collision with Lawson post-FP2, Verstappen said: "For me it’s not very smart behaviour when you’re in this position to pick a fight with me.” After the session, the stewards then gave Verstappen and Lawson a one-place grid drop for Sunday's Grand Prix, as well as a penalty point for an incident both drivers admitted was "unnecessary and clumsy." Permane says nobody was picking a fight Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Explaining what had happened in the build up to the incident, Racing Bulls boss Permane pointed to the drivers' need to warm up tyres in the final sector of the Mexico City GP circuit, with lock-ups constant after the long start-finish straight at Turn 1 during practice. "So, look, when you're doing a lap here, an out lap or a cool down lap, one thing that's really important is to do the last sector fast," Permane said. "Doing that gives you tyres for Turn 1. Without that, you risk front locking and things like that. They were both going for that, and I think if I describe it with one word, it's just unnecessary." Asked on Verstappen's comments, Permane did not accept the idea that his driver had gone looking for trouble. "That's not the case. I'm sure they've both got an opinion on it. item.description: (Photo by Jeff Spicer - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images) | UEFA via Getty Images Speaking to France Football (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ) following his historic triumph, Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane admitted that the significance of the award has not fully sunk in yet. For a player who has spent years establishing himself among the best in world football, finally receiving the sport’s most prestigious individual honor is an experience unlike anything he has encountered before. “I don’t think I’ve fully realized what’s happening to me yet. I’m still trying to take it all in. To be honest, it’s very difficult to fully appreciate the significance of su ch an important award, especially when you’re still an active player. It’s by attending events like these, seeing Cristiano, Mess i, and all the great legends of the past, that you begin to understand what it really means,” said Kane. Kane also opened up about t he emotions he experienced when Cristiano Ronaldo announced his name as the winner. Despite everything he has accomplished o n the pitch, the moment brought an entirely different kind of pressure. “I was nervous, really nervous. My heart was racing. It’s a very different kind of pressure from what you experience before a big match, when you know you can influence the outcome by playing well or scoring a goal. At the moment when Ronaldo was about to announce the winner, I felt as though he had dragged out the suspense for 20 minutes. When he said my name, all the emotions hit me at once: relief, happiness…I didn’t really know how to react. I was completely overwhelmed. I had never experienced anything like that before,” Kane remarked. There is something partic ularly special about hearing Kane describe the experience this way. However, what separated him from the rest was his refusal to back down when discussing controversial topics. He always tackled them head on, and that was the case back in 2016 when Dustin Johnson was on the wrong end of a farcical decision from the USGA. Johnson finally got over the line to win his first major championship in 2016 when he lifted the US Open trophy at Oakmont. However, his first major triumph certainly did not pass without incident. The Blues, on the other hand, were sitting fifth in the league table, but arrived at the game on the back of consecutive defeats against Liverpool and Tottenham Hotspur. United, as such, had the opportunity to take advantage of the London giants’ poor run. Carrick made three changes to the team that had lost 3-0 to Bournemouth last weekend, with Bruno Fernandes, Matheus Cunha and Lisandro Martinez replacing Youri Tielemans, Mason Mount and Ayden Heaven. Unfortunately, Lisandro Martinez picked up a red card as the Red Devils suffered a 2-0 defeat at Stamford Bridge, with Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer securing all three points for the Blues. Here are the four things we learned from the game. 1. United look better without Youri Tielemans Tielemans, who recently revealed that Carrick played a key role in his arrival at Old Trafford this summer, had started all 12 games across competitions this season ahead of this weekend’s game. However, the English manager opted to drop the 29-year-old to the bench and it soon proved to be the correct decision. Tielemans has been a shadow of his former self this season and, in his presence, United’s build-up play has been slow.
